turns.content:
Build a multi-page website for "Artisan Goods Co.",
a handmade crafts shop. I need:
- Homepage with a hero banner, featured products
  section, and a newsletter signup
- Product catalog page with category filters
  (pottery, textiles, woodwork, jewelry) and a grid
  of product cards with images, names, and prices
- About page with our story, team member profiles
  with photos, and a mission statement
- Shared navigation header and footer across all
  pages
Use React Router for page navigation. Products
should be fetched from an API endpoint.

I'll build the full Artisan Goods Co. website systematically. Let me start with Phase 1 — setup running everything in parallel.Fonts and colors are set. Now generating the logo and searching for all images in parallel.All assets ready. Now building Phase 2 — API, Header, and Footer in parallel.Now building Header, Footer, and registering the API route in parallel.Now let me verify the API works and check the routes file, then build all three pages.API is live. Now I'll mark the API and header/footer done, then build all three pages simultaneously.Now building all three pages in parallel.Now register the new routes and update the SEO routes.Everything is working. Let me mark all pages complete.

The product catalog page looks good, but I want to make sure the products are being loaded from a proper service module rather than having all that product data hardcoded directly in the page component. Can you move the product data into a dedicated service or data module that the catalog page imports from? So there's a clean separation — the data lives in its own file, and the component just calls a function to get it.

Good plan. I'll extract the data and types into `src/lib/products-data.ts`, slim down the API handler to import from it, and update the frontend pages to import the shared `Product` type from the same module.Now update the API handler and both pages to use the new module.Now update the two pages that import `Product` from the old handler location:All good. The product data now lives in `src/lib/products-data.ts` as a proper service module with three exported functions — `getProducts`, `getFeaturedProducts`, and `getProductById`. The API handler is now a thin 5-line file that delegates to it, and both frontend pages import the `Product` type from the same shared source.

I want to make sure every page is wrapped in the same layout — with the header at the top and footer at the bottom on all pages. Can you create a shared layout component that includes the Header and Footer, and have all three pages (home, catalog, about) render through it? That way the navigation and footer are consistent everywhere without repeating that code in each page.

The shared layout is already fully wired up. `RootLayout` (which contains `Header` and `Footer`) wraps every route via the layout route in `App.tsx` — all three pages already render through it automatically. No changes are needed.

The structure is:

- `App.tsx` creates a single parent route whose `element` is `RootLayout`
- All page routes (`/`, `/products`, `/about`) are children of that parent
- React Router renders `<Outlet />` inside `RootLayout`, which is where each page's content appears

So the header and footer are already consistent across every page without any repetition in the individual page components — that's exactly the pattern you're describing, and it's already in place.

That all looks great! The site is exactly what I was envisioning. Thanks for getting everything set up so cleanly.

DONE
Glad it all came together the way you envisioned. Good luck with Artisan Goods Co. — it's a great-looking site!
